I believe you're referring to the "Change Preventer" code smells, which are
design issues in software development that can make it difficult to make
changes to the codebase. Here are three types of "Change Preventer" code
smells:

   1. Divergent Change: This occurs when a single class is frequently
      modified for various reasons, such as adding new features, fixing bugs,
      or making changes unrelated to its primary responsibility. It violates the
      Single Responsibility Principle (SRP) and makes the codebase hard to
      maintain.
   2. Shotgun Surgery: Opposite to divergent change, this smell involves
      making many small changes across multiple classes whenever a single
      change in requirements is needed. It indicates that the code is tightly
      coupled and lacks proper separation of concerns.
   3. Parallel Inheritance Hierarchies: In this situation, a set of subclasses
      mirrors another set of classes with a parallel hierarchy. When changes

       are made to one hierarchy, they often require corresponding changes in
       the other, leading to code duplication and maintenance challenges.

These code smells should be identified and addressed during code reviews
and refactoring to improve code maintainability and extensibility.

                          Software Design & Architecture

State Machine Modeling:
                               State Machine Modeling is a behavioral modeling technique
used in Software Design & Architecture to represent the states an object can be in and how it
transitions between these states in response to events.
This approach is especially useful for modeling reactive systems like user interfaces, devices,
protocols, or game logic.

FOR MCQ:

State________ A specific condition or situation of an object during its life cycle.
Event________An occurrence that may trigger a transition (e.g., user input, timeout).
Transition________A movement from one state to another triggered by an event.
Action________A behavior that occurs due to an event or transition.
Initial State________The default starting point of a state machine.
Final State________The terminating point of the state machine

Why Use State Machines in Software Design?

 Clarifies complex logic through visual representation.

 Identifies all possible states and transitions.

 Simplifies testing and debugging.

 Helps in managing life-cycle of objects (e.g., orders, users, devices).

UML State Machine Diagram

A UML State Machine Diagram visually represents the states and transitions of a class or
system.

Basic Syntax:

 Rounded rectangles represent states.

 Arrows represent transitions.

 Labels on arrows show the triggering event and action.

Modeling Steps:

1. Identify the object or process to be modeled.

2. List all possible states the object can be in.

3. Define events that cause transitions between states.

4. Draw the state diagram using standard UML notations.

5. Add actions or activities that occur during transitions or inside states.

                                 Topic_78 & 79
                         Software Design & Architecture
                             (State Design Pattern)

Definition:
               The State Design Pattern is a behavioral design pattern that allows an object to
alter its behavior when its internal state changes. The object will appear to change its class.

When to Use:

Use the State Pattern when:

 An object must change its behavior based on internal state.

 You want to avoid large if-else or switch statements scattered across the code.

 You have many states with distinct behaviors, and adding new states should be easy.

Advantages:

 Simplifies complex conditional logic.

 Makes state transitions explicit and organized.

 Follows Open/Closed Principle (easily add new states).

Disadvantages:

 Increases the number of classes.

 Can be overkill for simple state logic.

                     Software Design & Architecture
              (Comparison of Strategy & State Design Pattern)

Strategy_______Defines a family of algorithms, encapsulates each one, and makes them
interchangeable.
State_______Allows an object to alter its behavior when its internal state changes.

 Strategy Pattern is about choosing algorithms externally.
 State Pattern is about changing behavior based on internal state.
 Both use the same structure (Context + multiple interchangeable classes), but differ in
  purpose and behavior control.

                                   Topic_81
                         Software Design & Architecture
                          (Composite Design Pattern)

What is the Composite Design Pattern?

The Composite Design Pattern is a structural design pattern used to represent part-whole
hierarchies. It allows individual objects and groups of objects (composites) to be treated
uniformly.

Benefits of Composite Pattern

   Simplifies code: clients don’t need to distinguish between single or group elements
   Supports complex structures (tree hierarchies)
   Follows Open/Closed Principle: easy to add new types of components
   Promotes recursion for handling structures

Drawbacks

 Can make code more complex when the tree structure isn’t necessary
 Might lead to a large number of small classes

Important MCQs

 Composite Pattern is a structural pattern

 Represents part-whole hierarchy

 Treats individual & composite objects uniformly

 Supports recursion and tree-like structures

 Downside: May cause extra complexity and many small classes

                         Software Design & Architecture
                           (Observer Design Pattern)

What is the Observer Design Pattern?
The Observer Pattern defines a one-to-many dependency between objects so that when
one object (Subject) changes state, all its dependents (Observers) are automatically
notified and updated.

Purpose:
           To establish automatic communication between objects. One object (the Subject)
maintains a list of observers and notifies them of any state changes, usually by calling one of
their methods.

Introduction to the Discipline of Design:
    We live in a designed world.
    Design is economically important and effects our quality of life
    Any product that is an aggregate of more primitive elements, can benefit from the activity
     of design.

Software Products:
    Software is any executable entity, such as a program, or its parts, such as sub-programs.
    A software product is an entity comprised of one or more programs, data, and supporting
     materials and services that satisfies client needs and desires either as an independent
     artifact or as essential ingredient in some other artifact.

What Is Software Design?
    Software design is the activity of specifying the mature and composition of software
     products that satisfy client needs and desire, subject to constraints.
    Software designers do what designers in other disciplines do, except they do it for
     software products.
    Design bridges that gap between knowing what is needed (software requirements
     specification) to entering the code that makes it work (the construction phase).

Design Occurs at Different Levels:

                                  Standard Levels of Design
Why Design is Hard?
    Design is difficult because design is an abstraction of the solution which has yet to be
     created

Design as Problem Solving:
    An especially fruitful way to think about design is as problem solving.

Advantages:
   1) Suggests partitioning information between problem and solution
   2) Emphasizes that there may be more than one good solution (design)
   3) Suggests techniques such as changing the problem, trial and error, brainstorming, etc.

Abstraction:
    Abstraction is an important problem-solving technique, especially in software design
    Abstraction is suppressing or ignoring some properties of objects, events, or situations in
     favor of others.

Importance of Abstraction:
   1. Problem simplification:
       Abstracting allows us to focus on the most important aspects of a problem in
        (partially) solving it.

   2. Structuring problem solving
       Top-down strategy: Solve an abstract version of the problem, then add details
        (refinement)
       Bottom-up strategy: Solve parts of a problem and connect them for a complete
        solution

What is Model?
    A model is an entity used to represent another entity (the target) by establishing
      a) A correspondence between the parts or elements of the target and the parts or
         elements of the model

      b) A correspondence between relationships among the parts or elements of the target and
         relationships among the parts or elements of the model.

Modeling:
      A model represents a target by having model parts corresponding to target parts, with
      relationships between model parts corresponding to relationships between target parts.

                          Target                                       Model

Modeling in Design:
    Modeling is used for the following purposes:
       1. Problem understanding
       2. Design creation and investigation
       3. Documentation
    Modeling work because models abstract details of the target.
    Models can fail if important and relevant details are left out.

Modeling in Software Design:
Software design models may be divided into two broad classes: static and dynamic models
   1) A static model represents aspects of programs that do not change during program
      execution.
   2) A dynamic model represents what happens during program execution.

Static and Dynamic Models:

    Static model examples include object and class models, component and deployment
     diagrams, and data structure diagrams.
    Dynamic model examples include use case descriptions, interaction diagrams, and state
     diagrams.

CS603 SOFTWARE ARCHITECTURE & DESIGN
             SHORT NOTES FOR MIDTERM
              SYLLABUS TOPIC 01 TO 76
             PREPARED BY ALMAS AFZAL

                                    Topic_1
                              Design (What & Why)

What is Design?
Design can be defined by two ways:
 As a Verb
 As a Noun

As a Verb: It is defined to make draw plans from something, for examples Clothes or
buildings.
As a Noun: It is defined as a drawing or sets of drawings showing how a building or product
is to be made and how it will work and look.

What is Software Design?
Software Design is the process of defining the architecture, components, modules, interfaces,
and data for a software system to satisfy specified requirements. It acts as a blueprint for
software development and ensures that the system is structured, maintainable, and efficient.

It includes design principles, patterns, and methodologies to create high-quality software

Why do we use Design?
We design things to improve situations, solve problems ans explore alternatives.

                                 Topic_2
                       Software Design (Objectives)

1. System Specification
System specification defines what the software should do.

It includes:

 Functional & Non-functional Requirement
 User Needs & Constraints
 Hardware & Software Requirements

2. The Software Design Process
The software design process is a structured approach that includes:

      Requirement Analysis – Understanding what the system should do.

      Architectural Design – Defining the system’s high-level structure.

      Detailed Design – Designing individual components/modules.

      Validation & Verification – Checking the design to avoid errors.

3. A Blueprint For implementation
Software design acts as a blueprint (plan) that guides developers.

It includes:

      Diagrams (UML, Flowcharts) to visualize system components.

      Architecture patterns (MVC, Layered Architecture) to organize code.

      Coding standards & guidelines to ensure quality.

During the design phase , software engineers apply their knowledge of:
 The problem domain
 Implementation Technologies

Basic Objectives of Software Design:
 It translates system specification into plans for the technical implementation of the
  software.
 It serves as a technical plan for implementation.
 It specifies the overall structure and organization of the eventual code.

The system or Program should meets the customer’s needs.

A Software Should be:
 Easy to Implement
 Efficient
 Easily Extendible to meet new needs

                             Topic_3 & 4
                  Software Design (Complexity & Size)

Remember that:
Poorly designed programs are difficult to understand & Modify.

Software design complexity refers to how difficult it is to understand, modify, test, or
maintain a software system. It depends on:

Code Structure – Messy or well-organized?
Module Interactions – Are components highly dependent on each other?
Algorithms & Logic – Are they simple or too complex?
Scalability – Can it handle growth easily?

Example: A simple calculator app has low complexity, while an AI-based chatbot has
high complexity due to advanced algorithms.

Software Design Size:
Software size refers to the amount of code, number of modules, and overall system scope.
It is measured using:

Lines of Code (LOC) – Total number of written code lines.
Function Points (FP) – Measures functionality based on inputs, outputs, and interactions.
Cyclomatic Complexity – Measures the number of independent paths in the code.

Impact of Size:
      Small-sized software is easier to develop and maintain.

      Large-sized software requires careful planning, modularity, and documentation.

                              Topic_5
               Software Design (types of Complexities)

1. Essential Complexities
Complexities that are inherit in the problem.

2. Accidental / incidental Complexities
Complexities that are artifacts of the Solution.

The total amount of complexity in a software design is:
Essential Complexities + Accidental / incidental Complexities

Design: is an Antidote to complexity

Design is a primary tool for managing essential & accidental complexities in Software.

                                  Topic_6
                       Why is Software Design Hard?

Why is Software Design Hard?
Software Design is hard because design is an abstraction of the solution which has yet to be
created.

                                     Topic_7
                                 Software Design
                               A science or an art?

Software design is considered both a science and an art because it involves structured
principles (science) and creative problem-solving (art).

 Software design is a science because it follows engineering principles.
 It is also an art because it requires creativity and problem-solving skills.
 The best software designs balance both aspects for efficiency and user satisfaction.

MCQ:

         Science is a repeatable process.
         For Example: 2 + 2 = 4

                               Topic_8
                  Software Design (A Wicked Problem)

A Wicked Problem
A problem that can only be clearly defined by completely solved it.

Software design is not just a step-by-step process; it requires continuous adaptation,
problem-solving, and decision-making. Since there is no perfect solution, designers must
focus on flexibility, scalability, and maintainability.

                                Topic_9
                             Design Process
                      More Systematic & Predictable

The design process can be made more systematic & Predictable through the application of:

   Methods
   Techniques
   Patterns
   All applied according to principles & heuristics.

                                 Topic_10
                    Dealing with Software Complexity
                       Different rules & Principles

There are two types of Complexities:
Essential Complexity
Accidental Complexity

    Design is economically important and effects our quality of life
    Any product that is an aggregate of more primitive elements, can benefit from the activity
     of design.

Software Products:
    Software is any executable entity, such as a program, or its parts, such as sub-programs.
    A software product is an entity comprised of one or more programs, data, and supporting
     materials and services that satisfies client needs and desires either as an independent
     artifact or as essential ingredient in some other artifact.

What Is Software Design?
    Software design is the activity of specifying the mature and composition of software
     products that satisfy client needs and desire, subject to constraints.
    Software designers do what designers in other disciplines do, except they do it for
     software products.
    Design bridges that gap between knowing what is needed (software requirements
     specification) to entering the code that makes it work (the construction phase).

Why Design is Hard?
    Design is difficult because design is an abstraction of the solution which has yet to be
     created

Design as Problem Solving:
    An especially fruitful way to think about design is as problem solving.

Advantages:
   1) Suggests partitioning information between problem and solution
   2) Emphasizes that there may be more than one good solution (design)
   3) Suggests techniques such as changing the problem, trial and error, brainstorming, etc.

Abstraction:
    Abstraction is an important problem-solving technique, especially in software design
    Abstraction is suppressing or ignoring some properties of objects, events, or situations in
     favor of others.

Importance of Abstraction:
   1. Problem simplification:
       Abstracting allows us to focus on the most important aspects of a problem in
        (partially) solving it.

   2. Structuring problem solving
       Top-down strategy: Solve an abstract version of the problem, then add details
        (refinement)
       Bottom-up strategy: Solve parts of a problem and connect them for a complete
        solution

What is Model?
    A model is an entity used to represent another entity (the target) by establishing
      a) A correspondence between the parts or elements of the target and the parts or
         elements of the model

      b) A correspondence between relationships among the parts or elements of the target and
         relationships among the parts or elements of the model.

Modeling:
      A model represents a target by having model parts corresponding to target parts, with
      relationships between model parts corresponding to relationships between target parts.

                          Target                                       Model

Modeling in Design:
    Modeling is used for the following purposes:
       1. Problem understanding
       2. Design creation and investigation
       3. Documentation
    Modeling work because models abstract details of the target.
    Models can fail if important and relevant details are left out.

Modeling in Software Design:
Software design models may be divided into two broad classes: static and dynamic models
   1) A static model represents aspects of programs that do not change during program
      execution.
   2) A dynamic model represents what happens during program execution.

Static and Dynamic Models:

    Static model examples include object and class models, component and deployment
     diagrams, and data structure diagrams.
    Dynamic model examples include use case descriptions, interaction diagrams, and state
     diagrams.

Varieties of Design:
    Product design is a discipline that arose during the Industrial Revolution and is now an
     established ﬁeld whose practitioners specify products.
    The major issues in product design are aesthetics, product features and capabilities,
     usability, manageability, manufacturability, and operability.

    Engineering design is the activity of specifying the technical mechanisms and workings
     of a product. Engineers apply mathematical and scientiﬁc principles and techniques to
     work out the technical details of complex products.
    Product designers and engineers often work together in design teams to specify large and
     complex products.

                          Product Designer vs. Engineering Designer

   1) Product designers are concerned with styling and aesthetics, function and usability,
      manufacturability and manageability.
   2) Industrial designers, (building) architects, interior designers, graphic designers, etc.
   3) Engineering designers are concerned with technical mechanisms and workings.

   4) Structural, mechanical, chemical, and electrical engineers
   5) Product designers handle the “externals” of product design while engineers take care of
      the “internal” technical details.
